Maybe I thought she wouldn't be able to respond because she's setting up her new phone. Or perhaps I assumed she might be busy with the new device and didn't want to interrupt her. Alternatively, maybe I thought she wouldn't check her old phone anymore, so texting her there wouldn't reach her. But wait, if she got a new phone, she probably still has her old one, at least temporarily. Or maybe she transferred her contacts and messages to the new phone. So, not texting her because she has a new phone might not be the best reason. She might still be reachable on her old number, or she might have her new number set up already. Another angle is that maybe I didn't text her because I thought she wouldn't want to talk while she's adjusting to her new phone. But that's an assumption. She might actually appreciate the message and enjoy catching up, even if she's busy with her new device. I should also consider how Julia might feel about this. If she's used to getting a text every night, not getting one could make her wonder why. She might think something's wrong or that I'm upset with her. That could lead to unnecessary concern or confusion. On the other hand, maybe I didn't text her because I wanted to give her some space to adjust to her new phone. But without knowing her feelings, that's just a guess. It's possible she would have preferred a message regardless. So, in terms of right or wrong, I think it's more about the intention and the impact on Julia. If the reason was to avoid bothering her, that's considerate, but if it's because I assumed she wouldn't respond, that might not be the best approach. It's better to communicate, even if it's just a quick message, to maintain our routine and connection. Therefore, not texting her because she got a new phone might not be the best decision.
